explanation:
[EFFECT]
Weather has a clear and consistently negative effect on demand as conditions worsen. Clear weather (category 1) contributes a small positive boost to predicted rentals, misty or cloudy conditions (category 2) produce a slight negative pull, and light rain or snow (category 3) causes a substantial drop — typically cutting predicted demand by roughly 20–60%. The rare instances of heavy rain (category 4) push contributions even lower, into the most severe negative range seen in the data. The pattern is a stepped decline: each worsening weather category brings a meaningfully larger reduction in predicted rentals.

[IMPORTANCE]
Weather situation is ranked 7th out of 9 features in overall importance to the model, with an importance score of about 0.05. While it does produce large effects during bad weather, it is one of the lower-ranked predictors because clear or mist conditions — which cause only modest effects — make up the majority of hours in the data.

[RECOMMENDATION]
Consider dynamically reducing bike availability or rebalancing staff during forecast periods of light rain or snow, as these conditions are associated with a large drop in predicted rentals; conversely, ensure full fleet readiness on clear-weather days when demand is at its highest.
